newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-EVERTON BEATEN TO SFORZA BY KAISERSLAUTERN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-EVERTON BEATEN TO SFORZA BY KAISERSLAUTERN.

text.p: Everton, desperately seeking a major international signing before the new season, lost out to German club Kaiserslautern in the race to sign Swiss midfielder Ciriaco Sforza on Monday.
Kaiserslautern, who clinched promotion to the Bundesliga last season, said it had paid 6.5 million marks ($3.6 million) to get Sforza from Italy's Internazionale.
The Swiss international played for the German side before moving to Bayern Munich in 1995.

Everton manager Howard Kendall, who last week failed to persuade Italian striker Fabrizio Ravanelli to join the premier league club from Middlesbrough, had said earlier in the day that he was close to signing Sforza.
But he was beaten to the signature by Kaiserslautern who are not one of Germany's most glamorous clubs but boast a fanatical following.
They won the Bundesliga in 1991 and have bounced back to the top flight after just one season in the second division with the help of former Werder Bremen and Bayern Munich coach Otto Rehhagel.

Kaiserslautern said Sforza, who has earned more than 40 caps for his country and took part in the 1994 World Cup finals, had signed a four-year contract and would join the team in pre-season training on Tuesday morning.
It was reported at the weekend in Britain that Everton had offered three million pounds ($5 million) for the Swiss player.

"We are very near to agreeing a deal," said newly-appointed Kendall who presided over the Liverpool club's glory years in the mid-1980s when they won the league twice and the European Cup Winners' Cup.
Kendall had hoped that the talks would lead to the player making a visit to the club this week. He may now turn his attention to other players before next month's start to the season.
Newspapers at the weekend linked Everton with Newcastle's Les Ferdinand after the England striker appeared to cast doubts on his future as Alan Shearer's strike partner at the club.
"We are looking for a quality striker and Ferdinand certainly is that," Kendall said. "Should he become available, we'd be interested. But that is not the case at the moment." $ = 1.787 German Marks)
